title: Nanochemistry
description: Carbon one atom thick, rolled, folded and caged. Unlocks graphene, nanotubes and buckyballs.

puzzle.goal: A nanotube is a strip of graphene rolled up so that the lattice vector n a⃗1 + m a⃗2 wraps exactly once around the circumference. The two lattice basis vectors of graphene have equal length and meet at 60°. Write the diameter of the tube using the dot product of the wrapping vector with itself.
puzzle.name: Carbon tube diameter from the chiral vector (n, m)
puzzle.form: sqrt ( ( n * vec ( a _ 1 ) + m * vec ( a _ 2 ) ) · ( n * vec ( a _ 1 ) + m * vec ( a _ 2 ) ) ) / π
puzzle.expr: a * sqrt ( n ^ 2 + n * m + m ^ 2 ) / π
puzzle.ask: With |a⃗1| = |a⃗2| = a and a⃗1·a⃗2 = a²/2 the diameter is a√(n² + nm + m²)/π. Find d (nm) for a (10,10) armchair tube with a = 0.246 nm.
puzzle.method: The circumference is the length of the wrapping vector; expand its square with the dot product of the two basis vectors. Diameter = circumference / π.
